title: Alignment Conserver listings can be changed immediately with no Forum post required
content:
A.1.13.1.3.2 defines the "Alignment Conserver Changes" Update Process for the Atlas's official listing of Alignment Conservers. Its triggers "can include, but are not limited to, recognizing a new Alignment Conserver; offboarding an Alignment Conserver at the request of that Alignment Conserver; adding an Alignment Conserver to the list of ACs who have received a formal warning; or derecognizing an Alignment Conserver for misalignment." The operative clause: "The Core Facilitator can modify the pertinent Active Data documents to reflect such changes immediately; **they are not required to create a post on Sky Forum**."

This stands out against the rest of the chunk, where nearly every discretionary act carries a publication duty — Direct Edits are Forum-posted, emergency multisig actions are Forum-reported, misalignment blocks get a written advisory opinion. Here the Forum step is explicitly waived.

The practical justification is plausible: the listing *is* the record, so the edit is self-publishing, and status changes need to take effect the instant they are decided rather than after an announcement. Derecognition in particular loses its force if it lags.

The cost is that the *reasoning* goes unrecorded even though the change is consequential — being derecognized for misalignment strips an actor's standing, and A.1.11.2.1.3 shows that Ranked Delegate status carries financial rights. The diff shows what happened, but nothing in this process requires an explanation of why, so accountability for the judgment depends on other provisions rather than on this one.
description: The Core Facilitator updates recognitions, offboardings, formal warnings and derecognitions for misalignment directly — the only Active Data process with no public-posting step.
